newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia frees 11 student activists in Surabaya.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia frees 11 student activists in Surabaya.

text.p: Indonesian police in the East Java city of Surabaya have freed 11 student activists linked with the group the government blames for July 27 riots in the capital Jakarta, a newspaper said on Sunday.

The Republika daily said the ll students, suspected of being involved with the activities of the outlawed People's Democratic Party (PRD), had to stay in Surabaya and report to police twice a week after being held by police since the middle of August.
"We put forward a request to free them two weeks ago. It was only granted on Friday evening," Indro Sugianto, director of the Surabaya Legal Aid Institute (LBH), was quoted as saying on Saturday.
The report said the police had accused the students and one teacher of being activists of the Indonesian Student Solidarity for Democracy (SMID), the student arm of the left-wing PRD.
It said one of the students was released on Wednesday and admitted to hospital with unspecified medical problems.

The daily said only three PRD activists -- Dita Indah Sari, Ponto and Soleh -- remained in detention in Surabaya. They were arrested in early July after the PRD's labour wing organised a large workers' protest in the city.
The government has accused the PRD of being behind the July riots in which the National Human Rights Commission found in a preliminary report that at least five people died and 149 were injured.
The official commission is expected to hand down its final report this week.
